investigation.title: Remote Agent Feature: Swarm Gateway 502 Causing Total Provisioning Failure Across All Remote-Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-10-08T12:41:30Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error: the production-api's POST /api/agents call could not reach the swarm gateway ELB at /v1/agents. Because the failure occurs at the very first network hop to the swarm backend, no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was ever collected, and all contract assertions remain unverifiable.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm gateway — the AWS ELB-backed backend that the production-api proxies agent provisioning requests to — was unreachable at the time of the eval run. Every remote-agent check calls POST /api/agents as its first step (evidenced by the runner branch at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1885 calling createAgent with machineType "remote"), and all three checks received the same 502 response with error code "bad_gateway" and the message "swarm gateway unreachable during agent provisioning: error sending request for url (http://[REDACTED].elb.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/v1/agents)". This is a shared upstream infrastructure dependency failure localized to the swarm gateway / ELB layer, not an eval runner defect or a contract misconfiguration. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is confirmed only at the eval observability layer.

possibleCauses: Swarm gateway ELB is down, unhealthy, or has no healthy targets registered in us-east-2 — the most strongly supported cause given the identical 502 across all three checks.
Swarm gateway ELB is reachable but the /v1/agents upstream service (swarm agent provisioning service) is crashed or not listening, causing the ELB to return 502.
Network routing or security-group change between the production-api and the swarm ELB that dropped connectivity at the time of the eval run.
Transient ELB connectivity blip that has since recovered — cannot be ruled out because no run history exists (previousRunCount=0, lastPassingAt=null).
Misconfigured or rotated ELB DNS/endpoint that the production-api is still pointing to an old or invalid address — less likely given the error message includes a live ELB hostname pattern.

investigation.title: Published Observability Snapshot Stale: snapshotAgeMinutes 596 Exceeds 300-Minute Contract Limit
investigation.summary: The eval for check `published-observability-snapshot` failed because the published status.json at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json was 596 minutes old at the time of the check (2026-10-08T12:42:07Z), nearly double the contract maximum of 300 minutes. investigation.rootCause: The snapshot file at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json was not refreshed within the required 300-minute window. The snapshot's `source` field reports `desktop-nightly-release`, meaning the last successful publish came from a desktop nightly release process rather than a GitHub Actions workflow. The most likely cause is that the scheduled or triggered workflow (or desktop nightly release process) responsible for regenerating and publishing status.json did not run, failed silently, or its output was not committed and pushed to the GitHub Pages branch for approximately 10 hours prior to the eval run. This is an eval-layer finding scoped to the snapshot publication pipeline; no evidence of a user-facing web outage is present.
proof: failed-check.message: 'snapshotAgeMinutes expected <= 300 but got 596' — the single violated assertion that caused the eval to fail.

failed-check.evidence: snapshotAgeMinutes=596, maxAgeMinutes=300, source='desktop-nightly-release', overall='major_outage', hasLiveSource=true, hasNonUnknownFeatureData=true — all other evidence fields satisfy their contract assertions; only snapshotAgeMinutes breaches its max:300 bound.
expected-output.contract: assertion { path: 'snapshotAgeMinutes', max: 300 } defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 482 — this is the earliest violated contract boundary.

source.infra/evals/status/features.json:383: check config shows statusImpact='informational' and required=false, confirming this is not a required check and does not constitute a declared service outage.

sibling.public-observability-page, sibling.public-models-page, sibling.public-marketing-pages: all three sibling checks passed, including the /observability route returning HTTP 200 — the web surface itself is reachable; only the snapshot data is stale.

possibleCauses: Most likely: The scheduled workflow or desktop nightly release process that publishes status.json did not run or did not complete successfully in the ~10 hours before the eval, leaving the previously published file in place and aging past the 300-minute threshold.

Second: The workflow ran but failed to commit or push the updated status.json to the GitHub Pages branch (e.g., a permissions error, merge conflict, or push failure), so the file on disk was not updated even though the workflow executed.

Third: The desktop nightly release process (source='desktop-nightly-release') is the only publisher currently active, and a gap in nightly release cadence (e.g., a skipped or delayed release) caused the snapshot to go stale beyond the eval window.
Fourth: A GitHub Actions runner or Pages deployment queue delay caused the updated file to not be visible at the public URL within the expected window, even if the workflow completed successfully.

Fifth (lower confidence): A configuration drift between the registry's staleAfterMinutes=360 (infra/evals/status/features.json line 383) and the contract's maxAgeMinutes=300 (infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 482 and line 486) means the eval contract is stricter than the registry staleness threshold by 60 minutes — a snapshot could be considered non-stale by the registry but still fail the eval contract.

investigations.rootCause: The swarm gateway — the AWS ELB-backed backend that the production-api proxies agent provisioning requests to — was unreachable at the time of the eval run. The snapshot's `source` field reports `desktop-nightly-release`, meaning the last successful publish came from a desktop nightly release process rather than a GitHub Actions workflow.
